descriptor: Transformer oils, white oils and Savsol lubricants
lede: A debt-free, 65-year-old Mumbai maker of transformer oils, white oils and Savsol lubricants whose profits swing with crude and base-oil prices. Q1 FY27 delivered more profit than all of FY26 thanks to inventory gains in the West Asia oil spike, which makes the trailing 12x P/E look cheaper than the business really is.

short_version.text: Record volumes above 5 lakh KL in FY26 (+17%), EBITDA per KL up to ₹4,555 and PAT +61% to ₹182 Cr (consolidated); Q1 FY27 PAT ₹288 Cr. No debt, ~₹508 Cr of cash and investments at March, an unbroken dividend record since 1994, and a growing premium ester-lubricant range.

Q1's 26% EBITDA margin came from inventory gains on a crude spike; normal margins have been 4-7% for three years, down from 12-13% in FY22. ROCE fell from 31% to 14%, cash conversion is patchy, and the company holds no earnings calls.
12.4x trailing earnings (inflated by Q1) and ~10x EV/EBITDA; on FY26 profit about 27x. Panama Petrochem trades at 6x, Gandhar at 9x, Gulf Oil at 14x.

blocks.text: Savita refines base oils and additives into petroleum specialties: transformer oils (Transol, the only maker of mineral, natural and synthetic-ester transformer oils), white and mineral oils for cosmetics, pharma and plastics, cable-filling compounds and waxes (73% of sales), plus Savsol lubricants for vehicles and industry (26%). It has four plants in Maharashtra and Silvassa, 53 MW of wind power, and exports to 75+ countries.

items.text: Margins depend on the spread between base-oil costs and product prices; inventory gains when crude rises, losses when it falls.
Transformer oils ride grid and power build-out; white oils ride personal care and pharma.
Savsol Ester5 lubricants grew 4-5x faster than the industry, premiumising the mix.
Commercialised its own synthetic-ester plant in August 2023.
Margins fell from 13% (FY22) to 5% (FY25) as base-oil spreads normalised; FY26 recovered to 6.6%.
Siddharth Mehra (son of the chairman) to become Joint MD from October 2026.

items.name: Bull
items.text: Volumes grow ~12% a year and margins hold above normal: revenue ~₹5,600 Cr in FY28 at a 6% PAT margin (₹336 Cr), valued at 20x, plus ~₹800 Cr of cash.

items.name: Base
items.text: ~10% growth to ₹5,300 Cr at a 4.5% PAT margin (₹240 Cr), valued at 18x, plus ~₹800 Cr of cash.

items.name: Bear
items.text: Oil prices fall and spreads compress: ₹4,800 Cr at a 3% margin (₹144 Cr), valued at 15x, plus ~₹800 Cr of cash.

blocks.text: Scenarios are illustrative, built on our assumptions, not company guidance.

A well-run, cash-rich specialty-oil business with a strong position in transformer and white oils. But Q1 FY27 profits are largely a one-off from the oil spike; on normal margins the stock is fairly priced, and the next leg depends on ester products and volumes rather than commodity luck.
